title: Second performance pass: optimize spec viewer timeline/map redraw CPU
Spec viewer re-applies the file-creation patch to the base doc, corrupting every snapshot
description: base_doc is the spec after patch 0 (the @@ -0,0 +1,8628 @@ creation diff), but reconstructSnapshot and computeAllMetrics start applying at patch 0. The creation hunk splices at index -1 and the >5000-line chunk path scatters a second copy into the document: the newest snapshot comes out at 26,860 lines instead of 18,232. Fix: treat base_doc as the idx-0 snapshot and apply patches from idx 1; make applySynapticPatch handle a zero-line old range (os=0) by inserting at the start; add a regression test.
close_reason: Fixed in viewer.tsx: base_doc is the idx-0 snapshot so replay starts at patch 1 (reconstructSnapshot and computeAllMetrics). Also found the reason the spec tab never changed: sql.js 1.14's browser build returns no rows for exec() with bound params, so getPatch returned '' for every patch; it now inlines a validated integer idx. Verified in Chromium: latest entry renders 18,232 lines with the Sept text; entry 136 renders 18,167.

title: Spec viewer patch engine inserts a blank line per patch, drifting snapshots
description: applySynapticPatch treats the empty string after a patch's trailing newline (and '\ No newline at end of file' markers) as context lines. Replaying all 136 patches yields 18,303 lines instead of the real 18,167-line spec, and the cumulative offset drift shifts later hunks. Fix: ignore the trailing empty element and backslash marker lines; add a regression test that replays a multi-patch history.
close_reason: Fixed in patch-engine.ts: trailing empty element and backslash markers are no longer treated as context; pure-insertion hunks (-a,0) insert after line a. Regression tests added (tests/unit/patch-engine.test.ts, 95 unit tests pass). Full 144-patch replay reproduces the engine HEAD spec byte-for-byte.
